thanks! I ran the [reference scenario SKILL](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/.github/skills/evaluate-reference/SKILL.md), can you review its findings?

## Credible reference coverage

- Span shape is correct: `chat gpt-4o-mini` wraps the `client.chat.completions.create(...)` call; request attributes set inline before the call, response attributes set from the returned object inside the same `with` block. Public entry point used.
- `gen_ai.response.model`, `gen_ai.response.id`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` are all direct off the OpenAI response.
- The `TextPart` half of `gen_ai.input.messages` is direct: it mirrors the `{"type": "text", "text": instruction}` content block.

## Too app-specific or cross-call — the central capture gap

The new scenario calls OpenAI with a `file` content block:

```python
{"type": "file", "file": {"file_id": "file-mock-kyc"}}
```

but emits a `UriPart` with a fabricated URI in `gen_ai.input.messages`:

```python
{"type": "uri", "modality": "document",
 "mime_type": "application/pdf",
 "uri": "https://example.com/sample-kyc.pdf"}
```

The OpenAI Chat Completions `file` content block exposes only `file_id` (opaque Files-API handle) or inline `file_data` (base64). Neither yields a URI at the SDK boundary. Native instrumentation watching `chat.completions.create` cannot honestly produce `uri="https://example.com/sample-kyc.pdf"` from `file_id="file-mock-kyc"` without a separate Files-API lookup (cross-call) plus app-specific knowledge that uploaded files originated from a public URL. The PR body even labels the S3/MinIO URI as an "offload-on-capture step", i.e. application-side, not library-side. This is a fabricated value, not a derivable one.

Similarly, `mime_type: "application/pdf"` is not on the SDK call boundary either — only `file_id` is. With an inline `file_data` block the mime type would be parseable from the data-URI prefix; with `file_id` it is not.

Two honest representations would be:

1. **Inline shape** — call the SDK with `{"type": "file", "file": {"file_data": "data:application/pdf;base64,...", "filename": "..."}}` and emit a `BlobPart` with `modality: "document"`, `mime_type` parsed from the data-URI prefix, and `content` from the base64 payload. Every emitted field then has a direct source on the call boundary.
2. **File-id shape (current scenario)** — keep the `file_id` SDK call but emit something honest: either drop the modality demonstration (file_id alone is not enough to claim document modality without a Files-API roundtrip) or emit a `UriPart` whose `uri` is the OpenAI file-id URN (e.g. `openai://files/file-mock-kyc`) and *omit* `mime_type`. The current emission is the worst of both — it claims more than the call boundary exposes.

Option 1 is the cleaner fix.

## Missing supporting library implementations

The PR body itself names two libraries with first-class document blocks. Neither received reference coverage, and both would demonstrate the new enum value far more credibly than OpenAI:

- **Anthropic** (`reference/scenarios/anthropic/scenario.py`). `anthropic.messages.create` accepts a `document` content block (`{"type": "document", "source": {...}}`) natively. The SDK call boundary directly exposes the document part, its source type (`base64` / `url` / `file`), mime type, and data. A `BlobPart` or `UriPart` with `modality: "document"` is directly observable — no fabrication needed. This is the canonical demonstration for this PR and is missing.
- **AWS Bedrock** (`reference/scenarios/aws-bedrock/scenario.py`). The Converse API accepts a `DocumentBlock` (`{"document": {"format": "pdf", "name": ..., "source": {"bytes": ...}}}`). `format` maps directly to mime type and `source.bytes` is the blob content. A `BlobPart` with `modality: "document"` is directly observable.

Google GenAI / Vertex AI also support PDF parts (`inline_data` with `mime_type: "application/pdf"`); worth considering as a third demonstration but not strictly required for this PR.

## Evaluation recommendation

1. **fix implementation** — the openai scenario should not fabricate a URI and mime type that the `chat.completions.create` boundary does not own. Either switch the SDK call to inline `file_data` (data-URI) and emit a `BlobPart` with all three fields directly derived from the SDK arguments, or scope the emission down to what `file_id` actually exposes.
2. **add reference for supporting library** — add an Anthropic scenario emitting `modality: "document"` from a `document` content block; this is the most credible demonstration of the new enum value and is explicitly cited as prior art in the PR description.
3. **add reference for supporting library** — add a Bedrock Converse scenario emitting `modality: "document"` from a `DocumentBlock`.

Without (1), the openai scenario shows the convention can be written down but not that native OpenAI instrumentation can actually populate it from a single chat-completions call. Without (2) or (3), the PR ships a new enum value whose only reference demonstration relies on fabricated app-side values.

The PR description says the OpenAI scenario uses a document URI part / file_id-based attachment shape, but this implementation emits a BlobPart (inline base64) and uses a `file_data` data-URI in the SDK call. Please align the PR description with the actual scenario (or update the scenario to match the described UriPart/FilePart approach) so readers aren't misled.
